stories.title: Nicaragua's President Ortega says there will be no more elections, extending his rule
stories.summary: Nicaragua's President Daniel Ortega declares "there won't be any more elections," cementing his grip on power and ending hopes for a democratic vote.

stories.title: Caitlin Clark's All-Star weekend comes with extra baggage
stories.summary: Caitlin Clark is playing some of her best basketball, but debates over her fiery style, flopping and on-court confrontations haven't gone away. The Athletic's Chris Branch breaks down her season.

stories.title: Justice Department is offering billions in new grants for police who partner with ICE
stories.summary: The DOJ is offering state and local police $3 billion to cooperate with ICE on federal immigration enforcement, part of a broader effort to expand the administration's mass deportation campaign.

stories.title: Food insecurity remains dire in Gaza despite fewer going hungry, report says
stories.summary: NPR's Debbie Elliott speaks with Carl Skau, acting executive director of the U.N. World Food Programme, about a new report on food security in Gaza.

stories.title: U.S. reports highest number of measles cases in 35 years
stories.summary: For the second year in a row, the U.S. has reported a record-breaking number of measles cases. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention on Friday said the country has now confirmed 2,318 measles cases -- the highest case count since 1991.

stories.title: Why the U.S. is losing the global sunscreen race
stories.summary: American sunscreens are way behind the rest of the world in terms of how well they prevent skin cancer. The Indicator's Darian Woods and Wailin Wong explain why.
